previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with symptoms of an acute asthma exacerbation triggered by a viral illness, presenting with chest tightness, shortness of breath, cough, and fever. She also had a positive urine culture for E. coli, but given her history of chronic colonization and ongoing doxycycline treatment for syphilis, this was not treated as an active UTI. Her respiratory symptoms improved rapidly with nebulizers, systemic steroids, and azithromycin. She remained afebrile and off oxygen overnight. Her supratherapeutic INR of 4.1 led to temporary discontinuation of warfarin, with instructions to restart after outpatient INR monitoring. She was discharged home in stable condition on a prednisone taper, azithromycin, and continued doxycycline, with follow-up planned for INR recheck and syphilis management.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  ___ morbidly obeses with h/o of DVT c/o of pain, redness swelling in
RLE concerning for cellulitis vs. abscess vs. DVT (given pt's hisotry) REASON
FOR THIS EXAMINATION: is there an abscess in right lower extremity or DVT 

COMPARISON:  None available 

FINDINGS:

Normal Doppler waveform with normal respiratory phasicity and normal
compressibility of the right common femoral vein, and proximal greater
saphenous vein, proximal deep femoral vein, proximal, mid, and distal portions
of the femoral vein, popliteal vein, as well as the posterior tibial and
peroneal veins.  No evidence of right lower extremity deep venous thrombosis. 
Significant subcutaneous soft tissue edema is noted in the right lateral
thigh, with skin erythema, most likely representing cellulitis.  No evidence
of drainable fluid collection or abscess.

IMPRESSION:

No evidence of right lower extremity DVT.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with Morganella UTI and cellulitis, needs PICC
for IV antibiotics.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ (radiology fellow) and Dr. ___
___ (radiology attending) who was present throughout and supervised the
procedure.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:

The patient was brought to the angiographic suite and placed supine on the
table.  Given previous difficulty getting central access on the left, we
elected to place a right-sided catheter.  Skin of the right upper extremity
was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  A tourniquet was
applied.  An initial ultrasound confirmed small basilic and duplicated
brachial veins.  The cephalic vein was the largest vein and this was targeted
for access.  Approximately 2 cc of 1% lidocaine were infiltrated into the skin
and subcutaneous tissues for local anesthesia.  Using direct ultrasound
visualization, a micropuncture needle was advanced into patent the cephalic
vein, ultrasound images were saved prior to and after venipuncture confirming
patency of the vein.  A nitinol wire was advanced through the needle and this
passed as far as the axillary vein without difficulty.  A small skin incision
was made.  Needle was exchanged for a 4.5 ___ peel-away sheath.  The
nitinol wire would not readily advance into the central veins, therefore a 40
cm 5 ___ Kumpe catheter was advanced over the nitinol wire and using a
combination of these two, the wire was positioned into the subclavian vein but
there was clearly another stenosis at this level.  The nitinol wire was
exchanged for a Glidewire which successfully traversed this stenosis and
passed into the SVC, right atrium and IVC.  Unfortunately, the Kumpe catheter
was not long enough to advance any further.  So this was exchanged for a
longer Kumpe catheter; however, this would not advance through the more
central stenosis.  Despite multiple attempts, we were unable to successfully
access the central veins, therefore following discussion with the referring
physicians, ___ midline catheter was placed.  The catheter was cut to 26 cm and
advanced over the wire after removing the Kumpe catheter.  The wire and
peel-away sheath were removed and the catheter was secured to the skin with a
StatLock device.  The catheter was aspirated and flushed without difficulty. 
The tip of the catheter is in the axillary vein.

IMPRESSION:  Technically difficult procedure due to multilevel central
stenoses.  A mid line was placed in the right axillary vein via the right
cephalic vein following discussion with the referring team.  The catheter is
ready for use.
